items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: I’m working with Pete Sokoloff who is our regular piano player with the Donnell Library band

ctx.x: It’s like a lunchtime sort of concert?

It’s a concert. It’s a concert. It’s a jazz concert. People come in who are either on their lunch break or retired people who are looking for something to do. And then also we © Fillius Jazz Archive -22-

were at The Cajun for 14 years which was a club, the last club in New York that featured classic jazz seven nights a week, and we also played there Wednesday at lunch. And they closed it down in August, they’re going to pull a building down. The place was making money and had good audiences, but they’re going to pull the building down and put up condos so that’s what happens. So I was able, luckily, to find another little restaurant in Greenwich Village called Greenwich Village Bistro and we can only — it’s a…
